notes: JAMB Use of English 2024 — 100 questions compiled from verified sources + style-matched items. Not official JAMB papers.

questions.prompt: From the passage, what is the primary reason breast milk is considered ideal for infants during their first six months?
options: It contains unique vitamins not found in other foods
It is tailored to meet their specific nutritional needs
It is less expensive than formula feeding
questions.explanation: The passage states breast milk contains vitamins, proteins, and fats “perfectly tailored to meet an infant’s nutritional needs” during the first six months.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the primary role of breast milk in protecting infants?
options: It provides a source of entertainment
questions.explanation: The passage says breast milk contains antibodies “that protect infants from infections and diseases”.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the primary reason skin-to-skin contact during breastfeeding is essential?
options: It reduces the risk of breast cancer
questions.explanation: The passage states skin-to-skin contact “fosters emotional security and attachment”.

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate goal of promoting and supporting breastfeeding, according to the passage?
options: To encourage mothers to breastfeed exclusively for the first year
To ensure infants gain weight rapidly
To improve the emotional well-being of mothers
To enhance the overall health and well-being of both infants and mothers
questions.explanation: The passage concludes that promoting breastfeeding is important “for the overall well-being of both infants and mothers”.

questions.prompt: In the context of the passage, why is breastfeeding considered a ‘natural practice’?
options: Because it involves feeding an infant with any available milk
Because it is recommended by healthcare professionals
Because it has been practiced since the dawn of humanity
Because it is the only way to provide nutrition to infants
questions.explanation: The passage notes breastfeeding “has been an integral part of human evolution”.

questions.prompt: Only those who have the calling to ______ knowledge are called great teachers.
questions.explanation: To “impart knowledge” means to communicate or pass on knowledge to others.

questions.prompt: They teach students various topics and ______.
questions.explanation: The appropriate collocation is “teach students various topics and subjects”.

questions.prompt: The teacher listens to their students express their worries and fears, yet the teacher has to pacify and ______ them through the right paths.
questions.explanation: The teacher pacifies and “guides” students through the right paths.

questions.prompt: As a ______ in the field of education, the teacher ensures that teaching-learning takes place.
questions.explanation: A “stakeholder” in education is someone with an interest or concern in the field.

questions.prompt: The teacher ensures that teaching-learning ______ takes place in and out of the classroom.
questions.explanation: “Teaching-learning process” is the standard educational term for the ongoing activities of imparting and acquiring knowledge.

questions.prompt: He/she is fast enough to move at the speed of the ______.
questions.explanation: “Speed of the genius” contrasts with the slow learner later in the sentence.

questions.prompt: In his care are the ______, the mark book and every other document which must be duly filled.
questions.explanation: The “register” is the document teachers fill for attendance and records.

questions.prompt: While at home, the teacher still plans his lesson and prepares his teaching ______.
questions.explanation: “Teaching aids” are materials used to support instruction.

questions.prompt: Teachers should not be brushed aside in the society as teaching is the profession that ______ other professions.
questions.explanation: The metaphor “birthed” means teaching gave rise to other professions.

questions.prompt: Teachers should be given a great ______ in the society.
questions.explanation: The passage calls for teachers to be given “great honour” in society.

questions.prompt: The manager’s tacit agreement was enough for the project to proceed.
questions.explanation: “Tacit” means understood or implied without being stated; unspoken.

questions.prompt: The witness gave a vivid account of the accident.
questions.explanation: “Vivid” means producing powerful feelings or clear images; graphic.

questions.prompt: Choose the option nearest in meaning to austere.
questions.explanation: “Austere” means severe or stern in manner.

questions.prompt: The principal was lenient with the students who came late.
questions.explanation: The opposite of lenient (permissive) is strict.

questions.prompt: His extravagant lifestyle led to his bankruptcy.
questions.explanation: The opposite of extravagant (spending too much) is frugal (sparing).

questions.prompt: Jemila’s austere reaction kept everyone on their toes. (Choose the opposite.)
questions.explanation: “Austere” means severe; “benign” means kind and gentle—the opposite.

questions.prompt: The teacher, as well as the students, ______ expected to be at the assembly.
questions.explanation: The subject is “the teacher” (singular); “as well as the students” does not change the verb.

questions.prompt: I have not seen him ______ the beginning of the year.
questions.explanation: “Since” is used with a point in time (the beginning of the year).

questions.prompt: Which of the following words has the same vowel sound as in seat?
questions.explanation: “Seat” and “key” both contain the /iː/ vowel sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letter in think.
questions.explanation: “Think” and “thought” both begin with the voiceless /θ/ sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the option that rhymes with taciturn.
questions.explanation: “Taciturn” /tæsɪtɜːn/ rhymes with “burn” /bɜːn/.

questions.prompt: Choose the appropriate stress pattern for embodiment.
questions.explanation: Stress falls on the second syllable: em-BOD-i-ment.

questions.prompt: Choose the appropriate stress pattern for declamation.
questions.explanation: Stress falls on the second syllable: de-CLAM-a-tion.

questions.prompt: The architect did the DESIGN. (Emphatic stress)
options: Was the design done by the engineer?
Did the architect destroy the design?
Did the architect do the draft?
questions.explanation: The stress on DESIGN asks “Who did the design?”.

questions.prompt: My only SON speaks like an orator. (Emphatic stress)
options: Does my only son speak like an illiterate?
Does my only daughter speak like an orator?
Does my only son read like an orator?
Does your only son speak like an orator?
questions.explanation: SON contrasts with “daughter”.

questions.prompt: Choose the option that rhymes with permit.
questions.explanation: “Permit” and “commit” rhyme.

questions.prompt: Choose the option that rhymes with boys.
questions.explanation: “Boys” /bɔɪz/ rhymes with “noise” /nɔɪz/.

questions.prompt: Choose the most appropriate stress pattern for productivity.
questions.explanation: Stress falls on the third syllable: produc-TIV-i-ty.

questions.prompt: Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letter in busy.
questions.explanation: The “u” in “busy” is /ɪ/, as in the first syllable of “vineyard”.

questions.prompt: Choose the option that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letters in archbishop.
questions.explanation: The “ch” in “archbishop” is /k/; “Christian” also begins with /k/.

questions.prompt: Who is the narrator of the story in the novel The Life Changer?
questions.explanation: Ummi is the narrator of the novel.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the university Omar gained admission into?
questions.explanation: Omar gained admission into Ahmadu Bello University.

questions.prompt: What exactly is the “Note of Salvation” from Ummi’s narration?
options: The cheat notes Kolawole Abdul passed to Salma
questions.explanation: The “Note of Salvation” refers to the cheat notes Kolawole passed to Salma during an exam.

questions.prompt: The quiet one in the text is ______.
questions.explanation: Talle is identified as the quiet one in the novel.

questions.prompt: The character referred to as the quiet one was named Talle because ______.
options: His mother died shortly after he was born
questions.explanation: Talle’s mother died shortly after his birth, hence the name.

questions.prompt: What is the status of Habib Lawal in the House of Assembly?
questions.explanation: Habib Lawal is the Speaker of the House of Assembly.

questions.prompt: At first, Salma did not like the ______.
options: Composition of her roommates in the hostel
questions.explanation: Salma initially disliked the composition of her roommates.

questions.prompt: The use of the expression “Notes of Salvation” is ______.
questions.explanation: It is a euphemism for cheat notes.

questions.prompt: The acronym “EMEC” as used in the novel means ______.
questions.explanation: EMEC stands for Examination Malpractice and Ethics Committee.

questions.prompt: How much did Dr Kabir Mohammed collect from Salma to cover up her EMAL offence?
questions.explanation: Dr Kabir collected ₦100,000 from Salma.

questions.prompt: According to the novel, Bint’s Social Studies teacher is ______.
questions.explanation: Bint’s Social Studies teacher is described as meddlesome.

questions.prompt: The narrator and her children sat ______ because the room was stuffy.
questions.explanation: They sat under the mango tree because the room was stuffy.

questions.prompt: It’s essential to pay attention to the ______ signals your body sends when you experience neck pain.
questions.explanation: “Subtle signals” fits the context of paying attention to early warning signs.

questions.prompt: While neck pain can result from minor ______ such as poor posture or muscle strain…
questions.explanation: “Minor issues” is the most appropriate collocation.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that rhymes with comb.
questions.explanation: “Comb” /koʊm/ rhymes with “home” /hoʊm/.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letters in hear.
questions.explanation: “Hear” and “heard” share the /ɜː/ sound in many varieties.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letters in smooth.
questions.explanation: “Smooth” and “clothe” both contain the voiced /ð/ sound.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letter in h(e)arse.
questions.explanation: “Hearse” has /ɜː/, as in “there” in some analyses.

questions.prompt: Choose the option nearest in meaning to candid.
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward.

questions.prompt: Choose the option opposite in meaning to obscure.
questions.explanation: Obscure means unclear; clear is the opposite.

questions.prompt: He is the man ______ car was stolen.
questions.explanation: “Whose” shows possession.

questions.prompt: Hardly had he arrived ______ the meeting started.
questions.explanation: “Hardly…when” is the correct correlative conjunction.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Correct spelling is “occurrence”.

questions.prompt: The synonym of abundant is?
questions.explanation: Abundant means plentiful.

questions.prompt: The antonym of transparent is?
questions.explanation: Opaque means not see-through.

questions.prompt: She is allergic ______ penicillin.
questions.explanation: “Allergic to” is the correct collocation.

questions.prompt: The plural of crisis is?
questions.explanation: Greek-derived plural is “crises”.

questions.prompt: He behaves as if he ______ the boss.
questions.explanation: Subjunctive “were” after “as if”.

questions.prompt: The idiom “to bury the hatchet” means?
questions.explanation: It means to end a quarrel.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Neither of the boys are here.
Neither of the boys is here.
Neither of the boys were here.
Neither of the boys have been here.
questions.explanation: “Neither” is singular.

questions.prompt: The word ephemeral means?
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived.

questions.prompt: I look forward to ______ from you.
questions.explanation: “Look forward to” + gerund.

questions.prompt: The synonym of obsolete is?
questions.explanation: Obsolete means outdated.

questions.prompt: The antonym of generous is?
questions.explanation: Stingy means unwilling to give.

questions.prompt: If it ______ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
questions.explanation: First conditional uses present simple.

questions.prompt: She insisted on ______ the bill.
questions.explanation: “Insist on” + gerund.

questions.prompt: The word meticulous means?
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail.

questions.prompt: The opposite of benevolent is?
questions.explanation: Benevolent means kind; cruel is the opposite.

questions.prompt: He prides himself ______ his honesty.
questions.explanation: “Pride oneself on”.

questions.prompt: The manager, together with his assistants, ______ coming.
questions.explanation: The subject is “manager” (singular).

questions.prompt: The word lucid means?
questions.explanation: Lucid means clear.

questions.prompt: She doesn’t like coffee, ______?
questions.explanation: Negative statement takes positive tag.

questions.prompt: The synonym of arduous is?
questions.explanation: Arduous means difficult.

questions.prompt: The antonym of scarce is?
questions.explanation: Abundant is the opposite of scarce.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: Double ‘l’ and double ‘n’.

questions.prompt: The idiom “a stitch in time saves nine” means?
options: Take timely action to prevent bigger problems
questions.explanation: Act promptly.

questions.prompt: The word pragmatic means?
questions.explanation: Pragmatic means practical.

questions.prompt: They have completed the project. (Passive)
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive.

questions.prompt: The synonym of tenacious is?
questions.explanation: Tenacious means persistent.

questions.prompt: The antonym of frugal is?
questions.explanation: Extravagant is the opposite.

questions.prompt: The ______ of the matter is that we need more funding.
questions.explanation: “Crux” means the central point.

questions.prompt: The word verbose means?
questions.explanation: Verbose means wordy.

questions.prompt: He is used to ______ up early.
questions.explanation: “Used to” + gerund.

questions.prompt: The synonym of resilient is?
questions.explanation: Resilient means tough.

questions.prompt: Each of the students ______ a book.
questions.explanation: “Each” is singular.

questions.prompt: The word impeccable means?
questions.explanation: Impeccable means flawless.

questions.prompt: He is good ______ mathematics.
questions.explanation: “Good at”.

questions.prompt: The plural of phenomenon is?
questions.explanation: Greek plural is “phenomena”.

questions.prompt: The idiom “to turn a deaf ear” means?
questions.explanation: To ignore.

questions.prompt: The word cordial means?
questions.explanation: Cordial means friendly.

questions.prompt: By the time we arrived, the film ______.
questions.explanation: Past perfect for the earlier action.

questions.prompt: The synonym of diligent is?
questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking.

questions.prompt: The company’s profits have ______ significantly.
questions.explanation: “Rise” is intransitive; past participle is “risen”.

questions.prompt: The word volatile means?
questions.explanation: Volatile means liable to change rapidly.

questions.prompt: ______ you like some tea?
questions.explanation: Polite offer.
